data.limitations: The main kernel study focuses on batch-1 decode and L40S. A100 does not reproduce the L40S speedup, so results depend on memory hierarchy and launch geometry. The 4B end-to-end result with an int8 output head includes a change outside the lattice weight kernel. Quality is measured on a limited set of models and tasks.
data.differences: Prior Leech-lattice quantization work emphasizes compression quality and did not provide the full multi-shell serving path required for the stated rate. This work implements that path and measures its GPU representation cost. Compared with QTIP, the unfolded lattice layout reads more bytes; compared with AWQ it targets a lower nominal weight rate but uses a more complex vector code.
data.implementation_status: An offline transcoder and fused CUDA GEMV are implemented and evaluated on L40S and A100 with Qwen3 models. The paper is arXiv v1 dated 2026-09-02.
data.research_positioning: This is a systems-oriented low-bit inference paper at the boundary between vector quantization and GPU kernel/memory-layout design. Its key systems lesson is that compression quality per file bit is insufficient: VRAM bytes per weight, decode regularity, and the target GPU byte bound must be evaluated together.
